# Unit test for function escape
def test_escape():
    class FakeMatch:
        def __init__(self, all, tail):
            self._all = all
            self._tail = tail

        def group(self, *args):
            if args == (0, 1):
                return (self._all, self._tail)
            raise AssertionError("unexpected group call: %r" % (args,))

    def make(tail):
        return FakeMatch("\\" + tail, tail)

    # Simple escapes resolve via simple_escapes
    assert escape(make("n")) == "\n"
    assert escape(make("t")) == "\t"
    assert escape(make("r")) == "\r"
    assert escape(make("a")) == "\a"
    assert escape(make("b")) == "\b"
    assert escape(make("f")) == "\f"
    assert escape(make("v")) == "\v"
    assert escape(make("'")) == "'"
    assert escape(make('"')) == '"'
    assert escape(make("\\")) == "\\"

    # Hex escapes
    assert escape(make("x41")) == "A"
    assert escape(make("x4a")) == "J"
    assert escape(make("x00")) == "\x00"
    assert escape(make("xff")) == "\xff"
    assert escape(make("x7f")) == "\x7f"

    # Octal escapes
    assert escape(make("101")) == "A"
    assert escape(make("0")) == "\x00"
    assert escape(make("7")) == "\x07"
    assert escape(make("10")) == "\x08"
    assert escape(make("777")) == "\u01ff"  # 0o777 == 511

    # Invalid hex escapes raise ValueError
    for bad in ("x", "x4", "xg", "x1g", "xzz"):
        try:
            escape(make(bad))
        except ValueError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("expected ValueError for '\\%s'" % bad)

    # Invalid octal escapes raise ValueError
    for bad in ("8", "9", "18"):
        try:
            escape(make(bad))
        except ValueError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("expected ValueError for '\\%s'" % bad)

    # Works with real match objects from the pattern used by evalString
    pattern = re.compile(r"\\(\'|\"|\\|[abfnrtv]|x.{0,2}|[0-7]{1,3})")
    assert escape(pattern.match("\\n")) == "\n"
    assert escape(pattern.match("\\x41")) == "A"
    assert escape(pattern.match("\\101")) == "A"
    assert escape(pattern.match("\\\\")) == "\\"
    assert escape(pattern.match('\\"')) == '"'

    print("test_escape passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":

    import re
    pattern = re.compile(r"\\(\'|\"|\\|[abfnrtv]|x.{0,2}|[0-7]{1,3})")

    def esc(s):
        m = pattern.match(s)
        assert m is not None, s
        assert m.group(0) == s, s
        return escape(m)

    # Simple escapes map directly through simple_escapes.
    for tail, expected in simple_escapes.items():
        assert esc("\\" + tail) == expected

    assert esc("\\n") == "\n"
    assert esc("\\t") == "\t"
    assert esc("\\\\") == "\\"
    assert esc("\\'") == "'"
    assert esc('\\"') == '"'

    # Hex escapes.
    assert esc("\\x41") == "A"
    assert esc("\\xff") == "\xff"
    assert esc("\\xFF") == "\xff"
    assert esc("\\x4") == "\x04"
